# Performance Evaluation of Wastewater Treatment Plant

Prashant P. Bhave1 & Shirish Naik2 & Shubham D. Salunkhe3

Received: 31 July 2019 /Revised: 22 January 2020 /Accepted: 24 January 2020 /Published online: 6 February 2020 # Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2020

## Abstract The present study evaluates the performance efficiency of a wastewater treatment plant. A sewage treatment plant operating on biological treatment method (Rotating Media Bio-Reactor) with an average wastewater inflow of 6 MLD has been considered for the case study. Wastewater samples were collected at different stages of treatment units and analyzed for the major waste water quality parameters such as biological oxygen demand (BOD), chemical oxygen demand (COD), total suspended solids (TSS), and biodegradability. The performance efficiency of waste water treatment plant along with the major secondary treatment unit as Rotating Media Bio-Reactor (RMBR) was calculated. The performance analysis on above two aspects was studied over 17 weeks. Overall performance was found to meet the design and discharge/effluent criteria as prescribed by the authorities. The studies of six units of Rotating Media Bio-Reactor (RMBR) over a period of 13 weeks have shown the reduction profile of the unit in treatment of wastewater with parameters of BOD and COD. The RMBR treatment profile is useful for the design and operation of the unit.

Keywords Wastewater treatment plant . BOD . TSS . Biological treatment . Rotating Media Bio-Reactor . Removal efficiency

In the European Community, only 21% of municipal wastewater treatment plants (MWWTPs) are performing well \[[6\]](#the-creek-discharge-standards-specified-by-central-or-wastewater-treatment-plant-in-the-southeast-of-spain-state-pollution-control-board-cpcb-or-spcb-11-chemosphere-155152162). In India, performance evaluation was carried out by CPCB, of 152 STPs located in different states all over the country \[[10\]](#the-creek-discharge-standards-specified-by-central-or-wastewater-treatment-plant-in-the-southeast-of-spain-state-pollution-control-board-cpcb-or-spcb-11-chemosphere-155152162). The total treatment capacity of all selected sewage treatment plants was 4716 MLD. After the study, it is concluded that the plant efficiency utilized was 66% \[[10\]](#the-creek-discharge-standards-specified-by-central-or-wastewater-treatment-plant-in-the-southeast-of-spain-state-pollution-control-board-cpcb-or-spcb-11-chemosphere-155152162). There exist only 51% of sewage treatment capacities in 35 metropolitan cities \[[10\]](#the-creek-discharge-standards-specified-by-central-or-wastewater-treatment-plant-in-the-southeast-of-spain-state-pollution-control-board-cpcb-or-spcb-11-chemosphere-155152162). plant design are the key factors that affect the efficiency of treatment processes. Performance assessment is important to know the effect of influent quality variation on the efficiency of treatment units. Therefore, to achieve these capacities existing treatment plant needs to be upgraded which requires performance evaluation to decide scope for expansion or pro- cess modification. These data of performance evaluation can be referred to during the design of the new treatment plant. The treated wastewater should be within the norms as given by Central or State Pollution Control Board (CPCB or SPCB) \[[2,](#the-creek-discharge-standards-specified-by-central-or-wastewater-treatment-plant-in-the-southeast-of-spain-state-pollution-control-board-cpcb-or-spcb-11-chemosphere-155152162) [11,](#the-creek-discharge-standards-specified-by-central-or-wastewater-treatment-plant-in-the-southeast-of-spain-state-pollution-control-board-cpcb-or-spcb-11-chemosphere-155152162) [12\]](#the-creek-discharge-standards-specified-by-central-or-wastewater-treatment-plant-in-the-southeast-of-spain-state-pollution-control-board-cpcb-or-spcb-11-chemosphere-155152162). Therefore, the objective of this study is to evaluate the performance efficiency of various units in the wastewater treatment plant at Charkop, Mumbai.

## Description of Study Area

The Domestic Sewage treatment plant located at Sector-8, Charkop, Mumbai, Maharashtra, India, is selected for the study. A well-planned system for sewerage exists in MCGM area. The total capacity of the sewage treatment plant is 6 MLD (Table [1)](#description-of-study-area).

The plant uses RMBR Rotating Media Bio-Reactor for biological treatment of municipal wastewater. After the Rotating Media Bio-Reactor (RMBR) unit, composite filter and ozonation system is provided. Ozone dose depends on biological oxygen demand (BOD) of treated wastewater. Normal ozone dose ranges from 5 to 10 ppm.

Samples were collected from the inlet and outlet of various treatment processes from sewage treatment plant. A total of 4 sampling locations are decided within the treatment plant. The samples were collected at 0-, 3-, and

## Methodology

In the initial phase of the study, the information and details related to treatment processes, working of plants units, information re- garding sludge disposal, etc. were collected for sewage treatment plant. Then, sampling location was decided from the inlet and outlet of different units of the treatment plant. The duration of the study is from October 2018 to May 2019, during which samples at regular interval were taken from each of the operating unit’s inlet and outlet respectively.

The performance of existing sewage treatment plants was evaluated by collecting samples from the sewage treatment plant and analyzing samples at Environmental Engineering Laboratory, VJTI Matunga, Mumbai, Maharashtra. The ex- periment involves the collection of samples by using grab sampling in clean plastic containers of 2-l capacity by follow- ing IS 3025-1 Methods of Sampling and Test (Physical and Chemical) for Water and Wastewater 1999. The sample stor- age is done as per the norms by the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) and EPA guidelines. The samples were ana- lyzed for various pollution parameters by conducting a labo- ratory test which includes total dissolved solids, total suspended solids, chemical oxygen demand, and biochemical oxygen demand as per standard methods.

Week 1

### Chemical Oxygen Demand

The maximum efficiency for the removal of COD was 96.35% which was achieved for week 11, and the least efficiency was observed at 68.42% for week 5 (Table [3;](#fig-2-cod-variation-cod-variation) Fig. [2)](#fig-2-cod-variation-cod-variation). In week 1, after RMBR COD is marginally in- creased due to unbalanced in chemical doses. The COD of wastewater before treatment is varied from 188 to 684.6 mg/l, and COD of treated wastewater is varied from 15 to 112.8 mg/l. The average COD removal efficiencies after Rotating Media Bio-Reactor (RMBR) and filtration unit are 59.98% and 69.18% respectively.

Biochemical Oxygen Demand

The maximum efficiency for the removal of BOD was 97.33% which was achieved for week 13, and the least efficiency was observed at 92.37% for week 7 (Table [4;](#fig-2-cod-variation-cod-variation) Fig. [3)](#fig-2-cod-variation-cod-variation). The BOD of wastewater before treatment is varied from 106.2 to 300 mg/l, and BOD of treated wastewater is varied from 5 to 11.2 mg/l. The average BOD removal efficiencies after Rotating Media Bio- Reactor (RMBR) and filtration unit are 62.85% and 72.14% respectively.

### Total Suspended Solids

The maximum efficiency for the removal of TSS was 97.62% which was achieved for week 15, and the least efficiency was observed at 89.47% for week 5 (Table [5;](#methodology)Fig.[4)](#methodology). The TSS of wastewater before treatment is varied from 380 to 500 mg/l, and TSS of treated wastewater is varied from 10 to 40 mg/l.

### Biodegradability

Biodegradability is the ratio of BOD/COD and is used to characterize the influent raw water. Depending on the value the raw water is characterized as bio-degradable or non-bio- degradable. This ratio helps to choose the suitable treatment process for the influent raw water (Table [6;](#methodology)Fig.[5)](#chemical-oxygen-demand). The values of biodegradability of inlet wastewater are var- ied from 0.25 to 0.81. During study period, the average value of biodegradability of inlet raw wastewater was 0.48.

The average COD removal efficiencies at 3-m length from inlet of Rotating Media Bio-Reactor for RMBR 1, RMBR 2, RMBR 3, RMBR 4, RMBR 5, and RMBR 6 are 36.57%, 32.52%, 41.52%, 48.58%, 44.58%, and 52.62% respectively (Fig. [6)](#chemical-oxygen-demand). The average COD removal efficiencies at 6-m length from inlet of Rotating Media bioreactor for RMBR 1, RMBR 2, RMBR 3, RMBR 4, RMBR 5, and RMBR 6 are 71.34%, 76.17%, 72.89%, 76.92%, 81.18%, and 84.17% respectively. The average COD removal efficiency of Rotating Media Bio- Reactor (RMBR) up to 3-m and 6-m length from the inlet of RMBR is 47.74% and 77.12% respectively.

The average BOD removal efficiencies at 3-m length from inlet of Rotating Media bioreactor for RMBR 1, RMBR 2, RMBR 3, RMBR 4, RMBR 5, and RMBR 6 are 64.45%, 61.02%, 61.28%, 61.09%, 69.55%, and 64.71% respectively (Fig. [7)](#conclusion). ## Conclusion

The study aimed to evaluate the performance efficiency of various units in the wastewater treatment plant. The results for week 11 and 17 are not considered for analysis and con- clusion as plant was under maintenance work during that pe- riod. The COD removal efficiency of overall plant varies from

68.42 to 96.35% during the study period. The lowest COD removal efficiency was observed as 68.42% for week 5 since during that duration certain units of the wastewater treatment plant were under maintenance. During majority of the study period the COD removal efficiency varied from 90.15 to 96.15%. The overall average COD removal efficiency of the treatment plant was found to be 92.65%. The BOD removal efficiency of overall plant varies from 92.37 to 97.33% during the study period. The overall average BOD removal efficiency of the treatment plant is 94.97%. The TSS removal efficiency of overall plant varies from 89.47 to 97.62% during the study period. The overall average TSS removal efficiency of the treatment plant is 93.27%. The average value of biodegrad- ability for inlet raw water in present study was 0.48. The average COD removal efficiency of Rotating Media Bio-

RMBR is 68.06% and 83.69% respectively. The average BOD removal efficiency of Rotating Media Bio-Reactor (RMBR) with filtration ratio up to 3 m and 6 m length from the inlet of RMBR is 90.50% and 95.24% respec- tively.
